newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand repatriates Burmese Shan refugees.
newsitem.headline: Thailand repatriates Burmese Shan refugees.

text.p: Thai officials said on Thursday they had repatriated more than 400 ethnic Shan refugees who fled fighting in Burma and sought a haven in Thailand three months ago.
An official at the provincial operations centre for displaced persons in this western border town told Reuters the operation to send back the 430 refugees began early in the day.
The refugees, mostly elderly women and including some children, fled from the northern Burmese Shan state into Thailand in March.
They were repatriated after officials said there were no more reports of fighting in their villages, said a source at the Shan Human Rights Foundation.
The official estimated that some 50,000 to 60,000 Shan people had crossed into Thailand over the past five months to work as cheap labour in Thai towns.
It was necessary to send back all such refugees, the official said, and the repatriation of further batches of people could be expected.
Thailand is faced with an influx of illegal entrants, especially from Burma and Cambodia.
The National Security Council has estimated that more than one million Burmese and Cambodians are living in Thailand illegally.
